newsitem.title: FRANCE: Renault to cut jobs in France in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Renault to cut jobs in France in 1997.

text.p: French car group Renault SA on Tuesday informed its works council of plans to cut 2,764 jobs in France in 1997 and plans to transfer another 1,032 jobs within the group, labour union officials said.

The French job cut plans follows last Thursday's sudden decision to close the Vilvoorde plant near Brussels in June, with the loss of 3,100 direct jobs in Belgium and another 1,000 jobs at risk at supplying companies.
The job cut plans were contained in information handed out to works council members ahead of a Thursday meeting with company management.
Earlier, a Renault spokeswoman declined comment to job cut reports but said the central staff committee would be meeting on March 13 to discuss an "employment plan" in France.

The programme would include "both a labour restructuring with internal transfers and the elimination of posts, as well as measures aimed at youth employment, with new recruitment to make up for early retirements," the spokeswoman said.
Renault unions have called a one-hour strike on Friday in all plants in France, Belgium and Spain to protest against the shutdown of the Belgian factory.
"We hope this is the beginning of a long period of labour struggle at Renault all over Europe," Daniel Richter of the pro-Socialist CFDT union said on Europe 1 radio on Tuesday.
